edits_summary: parseMarkdown.ts: Added optional `latexDisplay?: boolean` field to MarkdownSpan type (1-line additive, non-breaking).

parseMarkdownSpans.ts: Added higher-precedence `(\$\$([\s\S]+?)\$\$)` alternative as new groups 10-11 BEFORE the inline `$...$` alternative (now groups 12-13). Strikethrough renumbered 14-15, kbd renumbered 16-17. Added `handleLatexDisplayMatch` helper that pushes spans with `latex: true, latexDisplay: true`. Existing `handleLatexMatch` updated to read groups 12-13 instead of 10-11. Pre-existing guards (`isEscapedDollar`, `isPriceLikeDollar`) reused on the new display helper as well.

MarkdownView.tsx: Changed `<LatexRenderer ... inline />` to `<LatexRenderer ... inline={!props.span.latexDisplay} />` so display spans render with `displayMode:true` (KaTeX block typesetting) while inline spans keep `displayMode:false`.
rationale: Per BA root cause: the cycle 1 inline `$...$` regex (commit 0ba2ddfc) consumes the inner `$E=mc^2$` of any mid-line `$$E=mc^2$$` because parseMarkdownBlock.ts:150 only handles `$$` when `trimmed.startsWith('$$')`. Net effect: stray outer `$` glyphs around an inline-typeset KaTeX render, which the user describes as 'block latex broken'. Fix is a regex-precedence resolution: add `\$\$([\s\S]+?)\$\$` as a HIGHER-precedence alternative BEFORE the inline `$...$` alternative. JavaScript's regex engine tries alternatives left-to-right at the same starting index, so when the source has `$$` at position N, the new `$$...$$` alternative matches before the engine ever tries `$...$`. The lazy quantifier `[\s\S]+?` ensures multiple `$$...$$` formulas on the same line each match independently. The new `latexDisplay` discriminant on MarkdownSpan flows through MarkdownView -> LatexRenderer to enable `displayMode:true` (block typesetting). Block-on-own-line path (parseMarkdownBlock.ts) is untouched per BA's `do_not_touch` directive — it remains the ONE true block path; the new span-level path handles only the mid-line case that was previously falling through.
type_check_notes: yarn typecheck reports zero errors in the three modified markdown files. Pre-existing errors exist in unrelated files (SessionActionsNativeMenu.android.tsx, SidebarNavigator.tsx, SidebarAgentConversation.tsx, SidebarFileView.tsx) but are out of scope for issue 5.16.

diff_stats.justification_for_overage: Net +14 lines is within the 20-line minimum-diff budget. Two new symbols are required by the BA-specified approach: `latexDisplay` field on MarkdownSpan (BA-mandated discriminant) and `handleLatexDisplayMatch` helper (kept symmetric with the existing `handleLatexMatch` so both reuse the escape/price-like guards). Could compress by inlining the helper, but that hurts readability and reuse of guards.

regex_precedence_verification_mental_tes: Input `Block: $$E=mc^2$$.` -> at position 7, regex tries alternatives left-to-right. Bold `**` no; italic `*` no; link `[` no; code `` ` `` no; group 10-11 `\$\$([\s\S]+?)\$\$` matches `$$E=mc^2$$` lazily -> dispatches to handleLatexDisplayMatch -> span with latex:true, latexDisplay:true.

Input `inline $a^2+b^2=c^2$` -> at position 7, group 10-11 requires `$$` (two consecutive `$`), source has only one `$` here -> no match. Falls through to group 12-13 `\$([^\s$][^$\n]*?[^\s$]|[^\s$\d\\])\$` which matches `$a^2+b^2=c^2$` -> dispatches to handleLatexMatch -> span with latex:true (no latexDisplay).

Input `Inline: $a^2+b^2=c^2$. Block: $$E=mc^2$$.` -> group 10-11 (`$$...$$`) matches `$$E=mc^2$$` at position 30 (lazy, finds first closing `$$`). Group 12-13 (`$...$`) matches the inline at position 8 because groups are tried left-to-right at each position; at position 8 the source is `$a...$` (single `$` followed by content followed by single `$`) — group 10-11 needs `$$` so it fails; group 12-13 succeeds. Both matches occur in the same regex.exec loop iteration for distinct positions.

Input `Price: $100 USD` -> at position 7, group 10-11 needs `$$` -> no. Group 12-13 inline -> requires content not starting with digit (single-char case excludes digit via `[^\s$\d\\]`); even if multi-char content matched, requires closing `$` -> source has no closing `$` after `100 USD` -> no match. Stays plain text.
Input `Var: $name` -> at position 5, group 10-11 needs `$$` -> no. Group 12-13 requires closing `$` -> none -> no match. Stays plain text.
Input `Esc: \$x` -> isEscapedDollar guard returns true (1 backslash precedes `$`) -> guard branch falls back to plain text via pushTextWithAutoLinks. Same guard reused on display path.
